body.statement: For every fixed admissible baseline array \(B=(B_n)_n\), there is an array-dependent deterministic sequence \(\eta_n(B)\downarrow0\) with two separate conclusions. First, the sampling distance \(d_n^{\mathrm{samp}}(B)\), formed from the family of separately indexed laws \(\{\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}:\rho\in I,h\in H\}\), satisfies \(d_n^{\mathrm{samp}}(B)\le\eta_n(B)\); hence the sampling cdf conditional on \(E_{n,C}(\rho)\) converges to \(G_j^h(\cdot;\rho,\theta_j)\) uniformly over \(\rho\in I\), \(\theta\in[0,\pi/2]^J\), and \(h\in H\). Second, each \(\rho\)-indexed dataset \(\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho}\sim\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\) generates its own completion, kernel, cdf \(F^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,j}(\cdot;\rho,\theta_j,\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho})\), critical value \(q^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,j}(\rho,\theta_j,\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho})\), and distance \(d_n^{\mathrm{ref}}(B,\rho,\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho})\), and \(\sup_{\rho\in I,\,h\in H}\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\{d_n^{\mathrm{ref}}(B,\rho,\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho})>\eta_n(B)\}\to0\). Thus the random Fisher-reference cdf and critical value converge in their corresponding sampling probabilities to \(G_j^0(\cdot;\rho,\theta_j)\) and \(q_{\alpha,j}(\rho,\theta_j)\), uniformly in the displayed outer supremum. The permutation approximation uses the maximum-influence bounds derived in \(\mathrm{lem{:}derived\mbox{-}max\mbox{-}influence}\), while selected Gaussian ratio and anti-concentration bounds use the common lower margin \(\min\{\epsilon,\rho_0\}\) from the selection or variance premises and \(\mathrm{lem{:}derived\mbox{-}residual\mbox{-}scale}\). After \(\mathrm{lem{:}full\mbox{-}cell\mbox{-}factorization}\), the rejection probability under each \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\) converges uniformly to \(\Pi_j(\rho,\theta_j,h_s)\). No deterministic rate is asserted uniformly over all baseline arrays in \(\mathcal M\), and no finite-\(n\) covariance bound is inferred from the limiting \(\rho_0\) inequality.
body.justification: This is the load-bearing bridge from exact full-cell finite-population conditioning to the scalar Gaussian design criterion.
body.gap: Li--Ding and Shi--Ding control unconditional randomization statistics, while Tian--Taylor transfers iid laws through smooth randomized selection; none handles the complete signed cell, coupled without-replacement selector, random complement counts, studentization, imputed null reference, and moving selected quantile with one remainder.
body.consumer: It turns analytic Gaussian holdout choices into uniformly valid asymptotic full-cell conditional-power statements for finite randomized enrichment trials.
body.proof_tex:
Fix one admissible baseline array \(B\). All limits below are for this array; the theorem does not take a supremum over different arrays.

First consider one stage--\(1\) block, suppress its indices, put \(N=N_{n1s}\), \(m=m_{n1s}\), \(\delta=h_s/\sqrt n\), and write \(G\) for the random complement of the holdout. Hypergeometric variance gives, uniformly for \(\rho\in I\),
\[
\frac{g^1}{N}\longrightarrow\frac{1-\rho}{2},\qquad
\frac{g^0}{N}\longrightarrow\frac{1-\rho}{2}\quad\text{in probability}.
\]
For \(f_i\) equal to \(B_i-\bar B\), \((B_i-\bar B)^2\), or \((B_i-\bar B)(U_i^0-\bar U^0)\), the without-replacement variance identity and the fourth-moment bound imply
\[
\frac1{|G|}\sum_{i\in G}f_i-\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^Nf_i=o_{\mathsf P}(1)
\]
uniformly over all admissible complement sizes. The same conclusion holds after intersecting \(G\) with either treatment arm, because the arm fractions are bounded away from zero with probability tending to one. Hence the random arm variances converge to the full finite-population variance, the selector's exceptional totalization event has probability tending to zero, and
\[
X_{n,s}=A_s\sqrt{1-\rho}\,h_s+X^0_{n,s}+o_{\mathsf P}(1),
\]
where \(X^0_{n,s}\) is the variance-standardized complement contrast of the fixed \(B\)-values.

The corresponding rank expansion is also explicit. Let \(K_N(\delta)\) be the ordered-pair crossing count. The midrank identity gives
\[
\mathsf E\{\text{treated crossed-pair count}\}
=\frac{m(N-m)}{N(N-1)}K_N(\delta).
\]
Expanding the variance as a sum over two ordered edges, overlapping edge pairs contribute at most a constant times \(NK_N(\delta)\), while disjoint pairs have covariance of order \(N^{-1}\) and contribute at most a constant times \(K_N(\delta)^2/N\). Thus
\[
\operatorname{Var}\{\text{crossed-pair count}\}\le C\{NK_N(\delta)+K_N(\delta)^2/N\}.
\]
The pair-spacing assumption gives \(K_N(\delta)=O(N^{3/2})\), uniformly in \(h\in H\). Since the null rank-sum standard deviation is of order \(N^{3/2}\), the centered crossing term is \(o_{\mathsf P}(1)\) after studentization, whereas its mean converges to \(b_{1j}h_s\). Moreover, if \(d_i\) is the number of ranks crossed by unit \(i\), then \(\sum_i d_i\le2K_N(\delta)\), \(\max_i d_i\le N\), and
\[
\frac1N\sum_i\left(\frac{d_i}{N}\right)^2\le\frac{2K_N(\delta)}{N^2}=O(N^{-1/2}).
\]
Therefore the observed normalized ranks have the same limiting variance and covariance as the baseline midranks. Finiteness of the pair-spacing limit also forces the squared empirical mass of ties to vanish; consequently the normalized-midrank variance tends to \(1/12\). We obtain
\[
R_{1j}=b_{1j}h_s+R^0_{1j}+o_{\mathsf P}(1).
\]
The identical argument in stage \(2\) gives \(R_{2j}=b_{2j}h_s+R^0_{2j}+o_{\mathsf P}(1)\).

Conditional on a representative holdout, \((X^0_{n,s},R^0_{1j})\) is a fixed-dimensional vector of complete-randomization contrasts. The derived maximum-influence bounds apply to every scalar projection. The finite-population vector central limit theorem therefore applies conditionally on such holdouts. The preceding sampling identities show that the exceptional holdouts have probability tending to zero. A direct covariance calculation with the balanced sign \(W_i=2Z_i-1\), using \(\mathsf E(W_iW_l)=-1/(N-1)\) for \(i\ne l\), gives
\[
\operatorname{Corr}(X^0_{n,s},R^0_{1j})\longrightarrow\kappa_j\sqrt{1-\rho}.
\]
Indeed the complement indicator contributes one factor \(1-\rho\) to the covariance and one square-root factor to the selector standard deviation. The stage--\(2\) randomization is independent conditional on the history. Thus, uniformly over the compact parameter domain,
\[
(X_{n,s},R_{1j},R_{2j})\ \Longrightarrow\
\mathcal N\!\left(\begin{pmatrix}A_s\sqrt{1-\rho}\,h_s\\ b_{1j}h_s\\b_{2j}h_s\end{pmatrix},
\begin{pmatrix}1&\kappa_j\sqrt{1-\rho}&0\\
\kappa_j\sqrt{1-\rho}&1&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}\right).
\]
Uniformity follows by contradiction: any violating sequence of \((\rho,h,\theta)\) has a convergent subsequence; the uniform moment, share, and pair-spacing premises and the same central limit theorem apply along that subsequence. The residual-scale lemma prevents a singular projected limit.

The same reasoning applies conditionally to the Fisher reference. Under the realized local alternative its fixed completed value is \(B_i+\delta Z_i\). Its empirical second and fourth moments differ from those of \(B\) by \(o_{\mathsf P}(1)\). Its normalized ranks differ in empirical squared norm by \(o_{\mathsf P}(1)\) by the crossing-degree bound above. Candidate treatment labels are newly completely randomized and hence have zero contrast mean. Candidate holdouts are newly sampled independently, and candidate stage--\(2\) assignments are independent after the candidate cell is retained. It follows, in \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\)-probability and uniformly over \((\rho,h,\theta)\), that the pre-cell reference vector converges to the same Gaussian vector with all three drifts set to zero.

Joint convergence over rectangles and the fixed thresholds gives convergence of the corresponding numerator and cell probabilities. The sampling-selection margin and reference-selection margin bound the relevant denominators below by \(\epsilon\), deterministically eventually for sampling and with probability tending to one for the reference. Applying the conditioning-ratio lemma and the full-cell factorization yields uniform conditional-cdf convergence to \(G_j^h\) and \(G_j^0\), respectively.

It remains to justify the moving critical value. By \(v_j^2\ge\rho_0\), every limiting conditional score has a continuous positive density. Compactness of \(I\), the angle set, the primitive set, and the fixed thresholds bounds all null critical values in one finite interval: Gaussian tail bounds applied before conditioning give finite common lower and upper brackets. On a slightly larger compact interval the conditional density has a positive lower bound. The quantile part of the conditioning-ratio lemma therefore transfers the reference quantiles uniformly.

Let \(a_n=d_n^{\mathrm{samp}}(B)\); the preceding argument gives \(a_n\to0\). Let \(Z_n(\rho,h)\) denote the reference distance; for each \(\delta>0\), the argument gives \(\sup_{\rho,h}\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\{Z_n(\rho,h)>\delta\}\to0\). A diagonal construction chooses \(N_m\uparrow\infty\) so that, for \(n\ge N_m\), \(a_n\le1/m\) and the last supremum at \(\delta=1/m\) is at most \(1/m\); setting \(\eta_n=1/m\) on \([N_m,N_{m+1})\), and enlarging finitely many initial terms, gives \(\eta_n(B)\downarrow0\) with both asserted properties.

Finally, conditional on \(E_{n,C}(\rho)\), reference-quantile convergence also holds in probability because the sampling cell probability is at least \(\epsilon\). Decompose the rejection event according as the random critical value lies within \(\zeta\) of \(q_{\alpha,j}\); on the good event, its probability is bracketed by the sampling cdf at \(q_{\alpha,j}\pm\zeta\), and the limiting Gaussian anti-concentration makes the difference vanish as \(\zeta\downarrow0\). The resulting limit is the integral \(\Pi_j(\rho,\theta_j,h_s)\) established by the factorization lemma.
